chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the borrowed item, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no liability upon the borrower for the borrowed item when it perishes, if he was trustworthy'.

key_terms.الْعَارِيَّةِ: Gratuitous loan or borrowed item given for use without rent
key_terms.مَأْمُوناً: Trustworthy, implying no negligence or breach of conditions

ai.seo_question: What is the borrower's liability if a borrowed item is destroyed?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the borrower of an *'ariyyah* (gratuitous loan) is exempt from compensation (*ghurm*) if the item perishes while in their care, provided they were deemed trustworthy (*ma'mun*) and did not commit negligence or exceed the agreed scope of use. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that liability in gratuitous loans is contingent upon fault or breach of trust, distinguishing it from fixed-value loans (*qard*). The term *ma'mun* implies a presumption of integrity, shifting the burden of proof to the lender if they claim negligence.
